module.purpose: Computes aggregate scheduling availability by combining fixed-host and round-robin date ranges, removing duplicates, and filtering redundant intervals.
module.summary: This module orchestrates date-range intersection for individual, collective, and round-robin scheduling. It distinguishes fixed hosts from rotating hosts, applies out-of-office exclusions for team events, merges overlapping fixed-host ranges, sorts and deduplicates results, then removes ranges subsumed by broader intervals.
module.businessContext: Supports calendar scheduling by determining when all required participants are available. Incorrect aggregation can expose unavailable booking times or hide valid appointment slots.
functions: uniqueAndSortedDateRanges (~L8-22): Sorts date ranges chronologically and removes duplicate intervals.
getAggregatedAvailability (~L24-57): Aggregates participant availability according to scheduling semantics.

mutationOfArg: Sorts the input ranges array in place before filtering duplicates.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A single non-team availability input uses dateRanges rather than oooExcludedDateRanges.
given: const userAvailability = [{ dateRanges: [{ start: A, end: B }], oooExcludedDateRanges: [{ start: C, end: D }] }]
moduleContractTests.then: the returned ranges are derived from dateRanges and do not use oooExcludedDateRanges
moduleContractTests.rationale: Non-team availability must select the primary dateRanges field.

moduleContractTests.scenario: Multiple fixed hosts provide overlapping availability ranges.
given: const userAvailability = [{ dateRanges: [A], oooExcludedDateRanges: [A], user: { isFixed: true } }, { dateRanges: [B], oooExcludedDateRanges: [B], user: { isFixed: true } }]
moduleContractTests.then: the returned ranges contain only the intersection shared by the fixed hosts
moduleContractTests.rationale: Collective availability requires all fixed hosts to be available simultaneously.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A team event has fixed hosts and at least one non-fixed round-robin host.
given: const userAvailability = [{ dateRanges: [A], oooExcludedDateRanges: [A], user: { isFixed: true } }, { dateRanges: [B], oooExcludedDateRanges: [B], user: { isFixed: false } }]
moduleContractTests.then: the result intersects the fixed-host ranges with the non-fixed host ranges
moduleContractTests.rationale: Round-robin hosts contribute candidate ranges after fixed-host constraints are established.

moduleContractTests.scenario: The computed availability contains duplicate, overlapping, or redundant ranges.
given: const userAvailability = [{ dateRanges: [A, A, B], oooExcludedDateRanges: [], user: { isFixed: false } }]
moduleContractTests.then: the returned ranges are sorted, duplicate ranges are removed, and redundant ranges are filtered
moduleContractTests.rationale: The public result must be canonicalized before it is returned.

detail.name: uniqueAndSortedDateRanges
preconditions: Each range provides start and end values with a valueOf() method returning numeric timestamps.
postconditions: The returned array is ordered by ascending start timestamp, then ascending end timestamp.
No two returned ranges share the same start and end timestamp pair.
The input ranges array is sorted in place before the filtered result is returned.
invariants: Range uniqueness is determined by the pair of start.valueOf() and end.valueOf() results.
edgeCases: An empty input array returns an empty array.
Duplicate ranges with identical start and end timestamps are reduced to the first occurrence in sorted order.
Ranges with equal start timestamps are ordered by ascending end timestamp.
stateMutations: Mutates the input ranges array by sorting it in place.
detail.summary: Sorts date ranges by ascending start time and then ascending end time, while retaining only one range for each identical start/end timestamp pair.

specTests.then: Only one range for that timestamp pair remains in the returned array.
The result is an empty array.

detail.name: getAggregatedAvailability
detail.signature: export const getAggregatedAvailability = (userAvailability: { dateRanges: DateRange[]; oooExcludedDateRanges: DateRange[]; user?: { isFixed?: boolean } }[], schedulingType: SchedulingType | null): DateRange[]

parameters.name: userAvailability
parameters.type: { dateRanges: DateRange[]; oooExcludedDateRanges: DateRange[]; user?: { isFixed?: boolean } }[]

preconditions: Each userAvailability entry provides dateRanges and oooExcludedDateRanges arrays.
Date ranges are represented by the DateRange type.
schedulingType is either a SchedulingType value or null.
postconditions: Returns a DateRange array produced by intersecting the applicable fixed-host and round-robin availability ranges.
Returned ranges are unique, sorted, and filtered for redundancy.
The input availability arrays are not mutated by this function.
invariants: A scheduling type of COLLECTIVE or ROUND_ROBIN, or more than one availability entry, causes team-event handling.
For team-event handling, fixed-host and round-robin calculations use oooExcludedDateRanges.
For non-team-event handling, the selected host calculations use dateRanges.
Hosts with user.isFixed === true are excluded from the round-robin host set.
edgeCases: With no fixed-host ranges, the fixed-range intersection is omitted from the ranges supplied to the final intersection.
When round-robin hosts exist, their applicable ranges are added to the ranges intersected for the final result.
When userAvailability is empty, the function delegates the empty range set to the intersection and normalization pipeline.
A null schedulingType makes every entry eligible for the fixed-host selection, while the team-event condition still depends on the number of entries.
detail.summary: Aggregates user availability into a normalized set of non-redundant date ranges. It accounts for collective, round-robin, fixed-host, and out-of-office-excluded availability according to the scheduling type.

specLiterals.role: Identifies collective scheduling and enables team-event availability handling.
Identifies round-robin scheduling and enables team-event availability handling.

specTests.then: Fixed-host and round-robin calculations use each entry's oooExcludedDateRanges, and the resulting intersections are normalized into unique, sorted, non-redundant ranges.
Fixed-host availability is selected from dateRanges, and non-fixed users are included in the round-robin host ranges.
The returned DateRange[] contains the result after unique, sorted, and redundant-range filtering.
